Three years turning messy ledgers into decisions

I'm an FP&A professional with 3+ years of experience across financial planning, management reporting and business finance, currently managing ₹1Cr+ in funds and analysing ₹50L+ in monthly transactions. My work focuses on transforming financial data into actionable insights through budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis and decision-ready dashboards.

What I enjoy most is understanding the story behind the numbers—not just whether a forecast missed, but why it missed and what the business should do next. Outside my full-time role, I also help startups and growing businesses build financial models, reporting dashboards and automated MIS solutions that make decision-making faster and more reliable.

A4 Case studies

Selected work

Three real workplace problems, plus one investor-grade sample model.
Sheet1 — Fee Collection Dashboard

Excel-based management reporting & fee collection dashboard

Problem

Fee collection data was scattered across locations, dates and class groups with no single view for management.

Approach

Built a dynamic Excel MIS dashboard automating collection reporting with location-, date- and class-wise summaries and a KPI-based layout.

Result

Added percentage-contribution analysis so management could see which segments were driving (or dragging) collections at a glance.

Sheet2 — Budget Variance Analysis

Finance budget monitoring & variance analysis (SQL + Excel)

Problem

Leadership needed to know exactly where actual spend was breaking away from budget, and by how much.

Approach

Built a budget-vs-actual variance analysis solution combining SQL (MySQL Workbench) with Excel.

Result

Identified a ₹44,000 (4.1%) overall variance and flagged Operations running 67.82% over its budget allocation — supporting tighter cost controls.

MySQL WorkbenchSQLExcel

Sheet3 — Business Forecasting Model

Business forecasting & profitability model

Problem

A travel ticketing business needed a multi-year view of profitability as ticket volumes, salaries and rent all moved at once.

Approach

Built a 5-year forecast model across rail and air ticket segments, layering in margin, volume growth, salary increment and rental escalation assumptions.

Result

Modelled ₹1,31,81,900 in cumulative revenue and ₹36,75,260 in net profit over 5 years — air ticket sales carried most of the profitability even as rental costs grew 228%.

Financial ForecastingScenario ModellingExcel
Actual project infographic — click to view full size
Sheet4 — DCF & 3-Statement Model Sample project

DCF valuation & 3-statement financial model — Infosys Ltd.

Problem

Wanted a rigorous, investor-grade valuation exercise built from first principles rather than a template, on a company with public, auditable financials.

Approach

Built a 5-year unlevered FCFF model (FY27E–FY31E) with a CAPM-derived cost of equity, a 12.95% WACC and a Gordon-growth terminal value at a 4% terminal growth rate.

Result

Arrived at an intrinsic value of ₹952.87/share against a ₹1,155.10 market price (31-Jul-2026) — a 17.5% downside, read as fairly valued to slightly overvalued — and stress-tested it with a WACC × terminal-growth sensitivity table.
